title: J'ai, tu as…
en: The verb avoir (to have) — and how to say your age
intro: **Avoir** (to have) is the second most important verb in French, after *être*. French also uses it where English uses *to be*: for your **age** (*j'ai vingt ans*) and for feelings like hunger or cold (*j'ai faim*).

cases.label: tu as — you have (informal)
cases.rule: **tu as** /ty.a/ — for a friend, family, a child.

cases.label: il / elle / on a — he / she has, we have
cases.rule: **il a, elle a, on a**. **a** (has) has no accent; **à** (to, at) has one.

cases.label: ils / elles ont — they have
cases.rule: **ils ont, elles ont** /il.zɔ̃/ — you hear a /z/.

cases.label: avoir + people or things
cases.rule: To have something or someone: *J'ai un frère. Elle a une maison.*

cases.label: avoir + ans — age
cases.rule: Age uses **avoir**, and always **ans**: *J'ai vingt ans* (never “je suis vingt”).

cases.label: ne … pas de — not any
cases.rule: After a negative, **un / une / des** become **de** (**d'** before a vowel): *Je n'ai pas de frère. Ils n'ont pas d'enfants.*

cases.label: avoir faim, soif, chaud, froid, peur
cases.rule: Where English says *I am hungry / thirsty / hot / cold / scared*, French says **j'ai faim / soif / chaud / froid / peur**.

cases.label: ils ont or ils sont?
cases.rule: **ils‿ont** /il.zɔ̃/ = they have (you hear /z/). **ils sont** /il.sɔ̃/ = they are (you hear /s/).

cases.label: questions with avoir
cases.rule: Raise your voice: *Tu as un frère ?* In set phrases the verb comes first, joined with a hyphen: *Quel âge as-tu ? Quel âge avez-vous ?*

sections.title: 1. Avoir — to have
text: Like *être*, **avoir** is irregular: learn its six forms by heart.

head: Form
English
Sounds like
rows: il a · elle a · on a

examples.en: We have a house in Paris.

sections.tip: **il a** (he has) has no accent. **à** with an accent means *to / at*: *Il a une maison à Paris.*

examples.fr: {Elle a|av-il} une sœur et deux frères.
examples.en: She has a sister and two brothers.

sections.title: 3. Your age: avoir + ans
text: In French you **have** your age: *J'ai vingt ans* (literally “I have twenty years”). Never say “je suis vingt ans”.
Always add **ans**. To ask: *Tu as quel âge ?* (everyday), *Quel âge as-tu ?*, *Quel âge avez-vous ?* (polite).
sections.tip: Numbers link to **ans**: *un‿an, deux‿ans, trois‿ans, six‿ans* (/z/), *vingt‿ans* (/t/), *neuf‿ans* (/v/!).

sections.title: 4. Saying no: je n'ai pas de…
text: **ne** becomes **n'** before *ai, as, a…*: *je n'ai pas*. And after the negative, **un / une / des** become **de** — or **d'** before a vowel.
sections.tip: Only **un / une / des** change. With **être** nothing changes: *C'est un ami → Ce n'est pas un ami.*

sections.title: 5. Hungry, thirsty, cold… with avoir
text: For these feelings, French uses **avoir** + a noun, where English uses *to be* + an adjective.

sections.title: 6. Ils ont or ils sont?
text: These two sound almost the same. Listen for the middle sound: **ils‿ont** /il.zɔ̃/ (they have) has a /z/; **ils sont** /il.sɔ̃/ (they are) has an /s/.

sections.title: 7. Asking questions
text: The easy way: say the sentence and raise your voice: *Tu as un frère ?* In a few set phrases, the verb comes first with a hyphen: *Quel âge as-tu ?*

mistakes.why: After a negative, **un / une / des** become **de**.
**a** (has) has no accent; **à** means to / at.

story.title: Le questionnaire
story.en: In class, Tom and Inès interview each other.

lines.fr: Aujourd'hui, en classe, les étudiants posent des questions.
lines.en: Today in class, the students ask each other questions.

lines.fr: {J'ai|av-je} dix-neuf ans. {Tu as|av-tu} des frères et sœurs ?
lines.en: I'm nineteen. Do you have brothers and sisters?

lines.fr: Oui, {j'ai une sœur|av-have}, Carla. {Elle a|av-il} vingt ans. Mais {je n'ai pas de frère|av-neg}.
lines.en: Yes, I have a sister, Carla. She's twenty. But I don't have a brother.

lines.fr: Moi, {j'ai|av-je} deux sœurs. Et ma famille et moi, {nous avons|av-nous} un chien !
lines.en: I have two sisters. And my family and I have a dog!

lines.fr: Oh ! Et {tes sœurs ont|av-ils} quel âge ?
lines.en: Oh! And how old are your sisters?

lines.fr: {Elles ont|av-ils} douze et quinze ans. {Elles sont|av-vs-etre} très sympas.
lines.en: They're twelve and fifteen. They're really nice.
So, do you have all the answers?

lines.fr: Patience ! {On a|av-il} une pause dans dix minutes.
lines.en: Patience! We have a break in ten minutes.
Marc, a question: how old are you?

quiz.why: **a** (has) has no accent; **à** means to / at.

quiz.q: Léa et moi, nous ___ deux cousins.
quiz.en: Léa and I have two cousins.
Tom and Hugo, are you hungry?

quiz.q: Mes grands-parents ___ une maison à Marseille.
quiz.en: My grandparents have a house in Marseille.

quiz.q: How do you say “I have a sister”?

quiz.why: Age uses **avoir**, and you always add **ans**.
After a negative, **un / une / des** become **de**.
Hunger, thirst, heat, cold, fear: French uses **avoir**.

quiz.q: Listen: do you hear “ils ont” (they have) or “ils sont” (they are)?
